newsitem.title: USA: Arizona opens electricity revamp to municipal utilities.
newsitem.headline: Arizona opens electricity revamp to municipal utilities.

text.p: The Arizona Corporation Commission decided Monday to include municipal utilities in efforts to restructure the state's electricity industry.
The state regulatory agency modified a plan endorsed in October which would give customers a choice of electricity suppliers over a four-year period beginning January 1, 1999.
Municipal utilities could voluntarily open their markets to competition on the same terms as investor-owned utilities, getting an opportunity to compete elsewhere in the state, the commission said.
Companies will have to submit tariffs and rates to the commission for approval.
As of January 1, 1999, Arizona customers will be allowed to choose outside suppliers for up to 20 percent of their peak 1995 demand.
The percentage will increase to 50 percent in 2001 and and 100 percent on January 1, 2003.
Utilities will be allowed to recover costs for investments expected to become uneconomic under market competition.
